item.research_question: How can high-entropy materials (HEMs) leverage configurational entropy to overcome the limitations of conventional enthalpy-dominated catalysts, specifically regarding phase stability, active site tunability, and the breaking of scaling relationships in electrocatalysis?
item.material_system: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) including PtPdCoNiFeCuAuSn, PtPdRhRuCe, Ru0.44Rh0.30Co0.12Ni0.14, CoxMoyFe10Ni10Cu10, IrPdPtRhRu, Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, and AlNiCoIrM; High-entropy oxides (HEOs) and perovskites; Multimetallic nanoclusters (MMNCs).
item.processing_route: Carbothermal shock (ultrafast joule heating followed by rapid quenching at ~1500 K); Fast moving bed pyrolysis (FMBP) reaching 923 K within 5 s; Colloidal synthesis with seed-mediated coreduction and annealing at 600°C; Ionic liquid-assisted cosputtering; Ball milling and solvothermal synthesis.
item.test_conditions: Ammonia oxidation at 700°C; Ammonia decomposition at 500°C; Oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in acidic and alkaline media; Oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in acidic and alkaline media; Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic and alkaline solutions; Li-O2 battery cycling.
key_findings: Quinary HEA nanoparticles (PtPdRhRuCe) achieved ~100% conversion and >99% selectivity toward NO + NO2 at 700°C with no degradation over 30 hours.
HEA-Co25Mo45 catalyst reached a mass-specific rate of 0.74 gNH3 m−2 hour−1 at 500°C, representing improvement factors of ~24 versus bimetallic Co-Mo and ~19 versus Ru.
Computational models predicted an IrPdPtRhRu HEA composition with a ~40-mV lower overpotential relative to Pt (111) for ORR.
Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni nanoparticles with size less than 2 nm delivered ORR activity comparable to Pt under the same conditions.
Octonary RuIrCeNiWCuCrCo catalyst outperformed quaternary and binary counterparts in long-term operation for Li-O2 batteries due to higher configurational entropy.
GO-supported quinary HEA nanoparticles (FeCoPdIrPt) exhibited enhanced HER activity and stability in alkaline solutions relative to commercial Pt/C catalysts.
HEA catalysts containing five or more elements outperformed binary, ternary, and quaternary alloys in alkaline media due to broad adsorption energy distributions.
item.mechanism: Enhanced configurational entropy stabilizes single-phase solid solutions despite large enthalpic differences, allowing atomic mixing of multiple principal elements. Severe lattice distortion lowers the energy barrier for adsorption and activation, while the diverse local coordination environments and electronic perturbations (ligand effects) create a near-continuum distribution of adsorption energies. This distribution allows the catalyst to access optimal binding strengths for intermediates, breaking the linear scaling relationships that limit conventional catalysts.
item.limitations: Low surface area of bulk HEAs limits catalytic utilization; maintaining nanoscale morphology at elevated temperatures is difficult due to migration and aggregation; synthesis of single-phase HEAs requires overcoming thermodynamic barriers; characterization is challenging due to increased compositional and structural complexities; phase segregation can occur if entropy is insufficient to overcome enthalpic differences.
item.future_work: Further elucidation of structure-property relationships across different HEM subcategories; development of high-throughput synthesis and measurement tools for accelerated materials discovery; deeper mechanistic studies on surface restructuring under reaction conditions; optimization of catalyst stability for noble metal-free applications.
quotes: The ability to confine multiple principal elements in a single lattice is intriguing for the design of advanced catalysts with desirable activity, selectivity, and stability.
The broad adsorption energy distribution of the HEA catalysts partially covers more optimal binding energies for the intermediates, hence markedly boosting the ORR activity.
Counterintuitively, the entropy-stabilized single-phase state would be more thermodynamically favorable at even higher temperatures according to the Gibbs free energy equation.

item.research_question: How can the configurational entropy in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be leveraged to overcome the miscibility limitations of traditional alloys and enhance catalytic performance for complex reactions like ethanol oxidation?
item.material_system: Platinum-group metal (PGM) high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles containing Ru, Rh, Pd, Os, Ir, and Pt; specifically compared against physical mixtures of unary PGMs and binary/ternary/quaternary/quinary PGM alloys.
item.processing_route: Prepared using a facile polyol method to synthesize PGM-HEA nanoparticles.
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical ethanol oxidation reaction in aqueous solution; performance compared against commercial Pd/C, Pd black, Pt/C, and Au@PtIr/C catalysts; cyclic voltammetry used to analyze individual constituent contributions.
key_findings: The PGM-HEA nanoparticles exhibited much higher activity relative to commercial Pd/C, Pd black, and Pt/C catalysts.
Negligible activity was observed for the physical mixture of the six unary PGM nanoparticles, confirming the necessity of atomic mixing.
The PGM-HEA delivered a mass activity more than 1.5 times higher than that of the most active catalyst to date (Au@PtIr/C).
The PGM-HEA exhibited the highest current density in the full potential range compared to ternary, quaternary, and quinary PGM alloys.
Pt and Pd are active for ethanol conversion but become poisoned by adsorbed (CO)ad or CHx species.
Os and Ru facilitate the oxidation of (CO)ad, mitigating the poisoning effect for Pt and Pd.
Ir and Ru ensure that dehydrogenation or C─C cleavage occurs at a low potential, while further oxidation hinges on Pt and Pd components.
item.mechanism: The atomically mixed metals in HEAs play distinct yet concerted functions: Pt and Pd drive ethanol conversion; Os and Ru mitigate poisoning by oxidizing adsorbed species; Ir and Ru lower the potential for C─C cleavage and dehydrogenation. This synergy allows for efficient and complete oxidation of ethanol involving multiple proton-electron transfers.
item.limitations: The text notes that while simple reactions can be triggered by mono- and bimetallic PGMs, it is difficult to drive complex reactions involving multiple proton-electron transfers and intermediate species without the synergistic effects provided by HEAs.
item.future_work: The authors imply the need to better understand the contribution of each metal to the overall reaction, as demonstrated by their comparison of cyclic voltammetry curves of individual constituents to elucidate specific roles in preventing poisoning and facilitating cleavage.
quotes: The PGM-HEA nanoparticles efficiently catalyzed the ethanol oxidation reaction, exhibiting a much higher activity relative to that of the commercial Pd/C, Pd black, and Pt/C catalysts, respectively.
In stark contrast, negligible activity was observed for the physical mixture of the six unary PGM nanoparticles.
The atomically mixed metals in HEAs play distinct yet concerted functions that give rise to efficient and complete oxidation of ethanol.
